A DECISION THAT RESTATES A STANDARD MUST SAY SO ON ITS OWN ROW. Founder, 2026-09-30, reading DEC-0008: 'is this an exception? As we already have approved standards for fonts - 20 for heading, and so forth.' He had to ask because the row stated a rule and named nothing behind it, so it read as a new exception when it is his OWN amendment applied to two named tables. A changelog row carries no standard reference — only reading tells you which standard a row belongs to — so the link is declared here, by hand, and printed into the row's 'The standard that carries it' and 'EXCEPTIONS' columns. Keyed by decision identifier.

AND WHAT EACH DECISION GOVERNS (2026-09-30). Founder: “you have been [asking] me million questions wasting my time and energy without knowing what to do with it.” Measured, he was right: of the 33 decisions he answered on the wording-asks file, ONE named the figures it governs. The other 32 were recorded in his words, in plain English, and connected to nothing — so nothing could check that the app still obeyed them, and his time answering bought a record rather than a guard. Each entry below names the rows the decision governs, so a test can be written against it and the sync gate can see it. Where a decision is about HOW WE WORK rather than a figure, it names the standard that carries it and says so.

DEC-0008.standard_carrier: MoneyKeel/documents/standards/moneykeel_pres_spec_screen-design-standard_v01.md — the money-size row ("A money figure is at least 17 points. Reference tables may use 12 to 15 points", his amendment of 2026-07-15) and checklist item 5. The type scale it works within is theme.ts Typography.sizes: 11 · 13 · 15 · 17 · 20 · 24 · 30 · 38.
DEC-0008.exceptions: IT IS NOT AN EXCEPTION TO ANYTHING — it applies the reference-table clause his 2026-07-15 amendment already put on the standard, and names which tables count. It does NOT touch the 20-point heading rule (2026-09-14), which governs titles, not money. It is not an exception to the type scale either: 12 to 15 spans two scale steps, 13 and 15. Where the floor DOES bind: any money figure outside a table — a hero, a header trio, a figure standing on its own — is at least 17 points.
